column2: ...the wise one would live a hundred years and have no fear of thieves or enemies. Angry, he becomes gracious in battle by drinking mantra-water.
Collyrium and tilaka bring control; poetry arises at the tongue-tip; by reciting it sexual union is controlled; by reciting it, sight of the yoni (is controlled);
by touch one is controlled; by sesame oblation all is accomplished. One who eats food consecrated seven times has prosperity always.
This is the Ardhanarishvara form, Lakshmi and the Vaishnava and the rest. The power in the form of the Bodiless, and the second, tormented by Madana;
Pavanavega, Bhuvanapala — giver of all success. One should recite "Ananga, Madana, Anangamekhala" for prosperity;
on the middle petals of a lotus "hrim", the vowels and the ka-series for a woman; having written in a hexagon or on a pot, it is a means of control.
Om hrim chham, Nityaklinne, Madadrave, Om Om — the root mantra with six limbs, in a red triangle. Dravani, Hladakarini, Kshobhini, Gurushaktika;
in the northeast and the rest and in the middle, that Nitya; likewise noose and goad; skull, wish-tree, lute, and the red one with it;
Nitya, Abhaya, Mangala, Navavira, Mangala, Durbhaga, Manonmani are to be worshipped; Drava stands from the east onward.
Om hrim, to Ananga, homage; Om hrim hrim, to Smara, homage; to Manmatha, to Mara, to Kama — thus fivefold. The Kamas are to be meditated as bearing noose, goad, bow and arrows.

Rati, Virati, Priti, Vipriti, Mati, Dhriti, Vidhriti, Pushti — joined in order with Kama and the rest. "Om chham Nityaklinne Madadrave Om Om" — followed by the vowels and consonants from a to ksha (the alphabet is listed). "Om chham Nityaklinne Madadrave svaha" — the Adhara-shakti and lotus; the goddess on the lion in the heart and so on.

Om hrim kshum chhinda chhinda — the four thorns, Kalaratrika, in the northeast and so on and at the water-feet; Yamarajya from outside. Kali, Naravali, Kalinamakshamalini (names; mantra syllables garbled).
(Syllable-play of garbled mantra letters "mamodetattadomoma raksata svasva bhaksava; yamapatatayamaya matamo tata motama".)
(Garbled mantra letters "vamo bhurivibhumeya tata rishva shvari tata".) Outside Yamaraja, "vam tam" — the water of killing nature.
Collyrium joined with neem-resin, marrow, blood and poison; with a crow's feather as pen, in a cremation ground or at a crossroads,
one should place it beneath a pot, or throw it in an anthill; under a vibhitaka branch the yantra crushes all enemies.
One should write the Anugraha wheel on a white leaf or birch bark with lac, saffron, or crystal or sandal;
on the ground or wall, the name on the east petal in the middle compartment; in the section standing in water "Om hamso" or the pattisha;
one should write the Lakshmi verse, on Shiva and the rest, and in the order of Rakshasa and the rest (letter-squares: garbled "shri sama moma sa shri sanau yajne jneya nausa").
(Garbled letter-square "maya lila lali yama yajne jneya nausa maya".) Where it is to be known: outside, quickly, in the directions, the pot outside;
seated on a lotus, the lotus-wheel, conqueror of death, heaven-bearer; supreme peace of peaces, giver of good fortune and the rest.
In Rudra, compartments equal to Rudra should be made; one should write them there, beginning with Om and ending with "hrum phat", the first letter and then the next;
by the order of the knowledge-letters the name ending with "vashat"; below, this Pratyangira accomplishes all desires and aims.
In an eighty-one-place square, all by the order of the first letters; from the first to the last, the name ending in "vashat";
this is Pratyangira, and another, accomplisher of all works. One should write the Nigraha-anugraha (suppression and favor) wheel with sixty-four places;
she is the immortal and the knowledge: "krim sah hum" and the name in the middle; having placed a leaf beginning with "phat", one should enclose with three "hrim";
worn on a pot, the destroyer of all enemies, giver of all. Poison perishes by reciting in the ear, with the staff-mantras beginning with syllables.
Having worshipped the great tortoise, one should sprinkle the foot; one should strike with the left foot, remembering the enemy seven times;
then the stopping of the enemy arises, from redness of mouth. Having made the Bhairava form, one should write the garland mantra:

Om, Shatrumukhastambhani, Kamarupa, Alidhakari, hrim phem phetkarini — stop the mouth of my enemies, Devadatta and others, stop; stop the mouths of all those who hate me; Om hum phem phetkarini svaha phat. Having written the cause (name), at the end of reciting it the greatly strong; with the left hand one should write the mountain and trident, on the right hand

one should write the Aghora mantra; in battle it would stop enemies. "Om homage to the Lady Bhagamalini, throb throb, quiver quiver, Nityaklinne, flow flow, hum sah krim, svaha" — by this with gorochana and the rest one should bewilder the world by a tilaka.

Om phem hum phat, Phetkarini, hrim blaze blaze, bewilder the three worlds, bewilder, Guhyakalika svaha — having made a tilaka with this, subjugation of kings and the rest. Having taken donkey dust and a flower of a birth-impure person,
one should throw woman's menstrual matter at night on a bed and the like; it causes hatred. Cow's hoof and horn, and horse's hoof likewise,
snake's head, compressed — in houses causes banishing. Yellow oleander root with mustard — for killing;
blood of a snake and musk rat; oleander for that purpose; lizard, bee, crab and scorpion,

powdered and put in oil — anointing with it causes leprosy. "Om, to Navagraha: accomplish all my enemies, kill kill, Om so mam vum chum Om sham vam kem Om svaha" — with this, having worshipped with a hundred arka flowers one should place it in a cremation ground,

on birch bark or an image, for the killing of the enemy: "the planets". "Om Kunjari, Brahmani; Om Manjari, Maheshvari; Om Vetali, Kaumari; Om Kali, Vaishnavi; Om Aghora, Varahi; Om Vetali, Indrani, Urvashi; Om Jayani, Yakshini — O nine Mothers, seize my enemy, seize" — having written the enemy's name on birch bark, worshipped in a cremation ground, he would die.
The second is the Sadyo-gods and the heart with limbs. Know the fourth as the head, Ishvara by name;
the Uhaka is to be known as the crest, joined with Vishvarupa; its mantra is declared eighth, the eye is held tenth;
the weapon is declared the Moon; named Shiva, with Shikhi's banner; "namah, svaha, vaushat, hum, phat" in order;
of the heart and the rest with "jati phat" I declare the Prasada mantra: counted as Rudra from Ishana, one should draw up, colored with rays;
with a head pressed with herbs, standing above Uhaka; half-moon and half-nada, between two bindus;
at its end Vishvarupa, bent in three ways. So the Prasada mantra is the mantra doing all works.
Having drawn up the crest-seed and ending with "phat" — "phat"; the half-moon seat is to be known, Kamadeva with the serpent;
the Mahapashupata weapon crushes all wicked ones. The Prasada is told with parts; now the partless is told:
the herb, Vishvarupa, called Rudra, the solar disc; half-moon joined with nada, "visamjna", then bent;
the partless is for enjoyment and liberation; this five-limbed Sadashiva; radiant, Vishvarupa, covered, colored by void;
free of Brahma-limbs, void, his form a tree of essence; worshipped by children and the simple, it is for removal of obstacles.
The radiant one called Vishvarupa standing above Uhaka, rich in parts, of the whole — worship-limbs and the rest everywhere;
Narasimha standing in the end (Yama-place), life of the splendid, going to the head; the radiant mounted by Uhaka, lower half adorned by itself;
ending in half-moon and nada, adorned with Brahma and Vishnu; the ocean and Narasimha, divided by the solar measure;
when it is made, then his Brahma-limbs as before. One should extract the first letter called Oja joined with the radiant;
the radiant pressed by the radiant, the second letter chief; the radiant Ishvara likewise, third, giver of liberation;
the Uhaka pressed by the radiant, Varuna, Prana and Taijasa; the fifth is declared, then the Krtanta;
the radiant, water-breath, the seventh letter extracted; a lotus pressed by the moon, Nandisha bearing one foot;
the first should be joined at the end, the ten-seeded Kshapana; half of this and the third, fifth and seventh;
Sadyojata the ninth; from the second the heart and the rest; the ten-syllable Pranava ending with "phat" one should extract as the weapon;
the Brahma-limbs are joined with "namaskara" here, not otherwise. From the second up to eight, eight are held the Vidyeshvaras:
Anantesha and Sukshma, and the third Shivottama; Ekamurti, Ekarupa, and another Trimurti,
Shrikantha and Shikhandin — the eight Vidyeshvaras are remembered; from Shikhandin to Ananta the forms of the mantra-ends are told.
In a triangle a four-footed (diagram), one should draw a three-petalled lotus; at its back the road-division, a three-petalled Ashvayuk;
the foot-border with three-petalled lotuses by Vasudeva's sons; above it the altar should be given of a span's measure;
the door a lotus in measure; the sub-door is described from the compartment; the mandala made of door and sub-door is the destroyer of obstacles.
A red lotus in the middle, outer lotuses beyond; a white path should be made, and doors as one wishes;
the pericarp should be yellow-colored, likewise the filaments again. The mandala called Vighnamarda: in the middle one should worship Ganapati.
The name at the beginning with the boon, joined with Indra by the god; head struck by Tatpurusha; beginning with Om and ending with "namah";
called Gaja, Gajashirsha, Gangeya, Ganayaka, Triravarta, lord of heavenly Ganga, in the east row;
Vichitramsha, Mahakaya, Lambaushtha, Lambakarnaka, Lambodara, Mahabhaga, Vikrita, beloved of Parvati;
Bhayavaha, Bhadra, Bhagana, Bhayasudana — these twelve in the ten rows, Devatrasa in the west;
Mahanada, Bhasvara, Vighnaraja, Ganadhipa; Udbhata, Svanabha, Chanda, Mahashunda, Bhimaka;
Manmatha, Madhusudana, Sundara, Bhavapushtaka; in the north Brahmeshvara, Brahma, Manovritti and Samlaya;
Laya, Dutyapriya, Laulya, Vikarna, Vatsala; Kritanta and Kaladanda — one should worship, and the pot as before.
One should recite the mantra ten thousand times and offer a tenth; for the rest with ten oblations offer after recitation;
having given the full oblation one should perform the consecration, and all succeeds. A man should perform the teacher's worship with land, horses, elephants, cloth and the like.
One should recite a lakh; the garland of letters from head to shoulders, from "a" to "ksha," one should remember as entering like a human.
